diagnosis.observed_sequence: The conventional controller resolved the visible effect of a prior transport and issued inspect. The supervisor rejected inspect because its previous command was still outstanding; six simulated milliseconds later it consumed the prior terminal feedback. The rejection was retained in the registry but not delivered to the conventional controller, which remained pending and later requested help.
diagnosis.source_supported_mechanism: ContinuousAdapter.busy reads the newer owner snapshot, whereas the supervisor active_command is cleared only when terminal feedback is drained and processed. The original conventional_step gates on adapter.busy but not active_command. Its command method rejects outstanding work before native submission; its exception/failed path persists rejection without baseline.accept_feedback. The host loop can reach this decision after a finite drain batch while the independently ticking owner has advanced.
diagnosis.inference_limit: The event order, distinct native/journal times and source gates support this scheduling race. The retained journal does not record the exact thread interleaving or drain-batch membership. No claim identifies OS scheduling, fsync, device latency or noise as the unique cause.
diagnosis.feedback_identity: When the prior transport terminal arrives, Candidate.accept_feedback only updates the pending record for a matching request ID. The pending request has become inspect; the earlier transport receipt cannot fill its missing rejection.
diagnosis.physics_timing: All six owner timing and resource checks passed. This was a command-admission correctness failure, not an observed strict timing failure.
